Model C: freight forecast improvement study

Frozen validation choices

H3Shallow weighted Random Forest48 completed errors; none
H6Matched no-change baseline48 completed errors; volatility_6m
H12Regularized median boosting48 completed errors; none

What changed

Estimators now fit all eligible recent history, rather than discarding the latest 24 labels for a calibration holdout. The last ten years are used with greater weight on recent observations. Intervals come from past out-of-sample forecast errors; pre-2020 validation chooses the error window and whether observed freight volatility scales those errors. The matched no-change baseline uses the identical calibration rule.

The 2020-2021 and later periods were already inspected during the previous study. These are reused historical tests, not a new untouched holdout. Actual release dates and historical revision vintages remain unverified. No new source observations or predictor columns were invented.

Outcome: partial gains, no replacement promoted

The new H3 selection improves validation MIS, but disruption coverage falls from 87.5% to 79.2%. Its disruption MIS is worse. Retain the original study as the main reference.

The new linear H6 candidate has disruption median error 5.44% and coverage 83.3%. That is a useful improvement in the central forecast, but coverage remains below 90% and it does not beat its matched baseline MIS. Later median error rises to 11.58%, so this improvement is not consistent across periods.

No new candidate passes all H3/H6 historical probability gates. The optional RMS calibration extension did not improve the frozen selections. These artifacts are research experiments, not recommended production replacements.

Evaluation

Coverage must reach 90%; MIS should be below both the equally calibrated matched baseline and the strongest baseline selected using validation. A coverage + MIS pass does not include the separate recovery requirement. H12 is reporting-only.
